pos.personaBrief: Verified: Van Gaal 'believed in playing attractive attacking football based on possession', so his Ajax and Barcelona sides were built to keep the ball and control games through it.

pro.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, his possession game (verified) relied on patient, secure ball circulation from the back with set patterns, not direct long balls.

est.personaBrief: Verified: 'set patterns of play inspired by Dutch total football' at Ajax; from general knowledge this meant a rigid positional 4-3-3/3-4-3 where every player held a defined zone, wingers stayed wide and the striker was the fixed point.

lar.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge his Ajax and Barcelona sides used touchline wingers (Overmars, Finidi, Figo) to stretch play, consistent with the verified total-football structure.

blo.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis, open question on Ajax pressing); from general knowledge his Ajax pressed high and won the ball back quickly in the opponent's half, in line with total-football principles (verified).

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge his teams defended zonally, covering spaces within the positional structure rather than man-marking.

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge Van Gaal imposed his own game model ('set patterns', verified) on every club and opponent, with players fitting the system.

res.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); the verified 'attractive attacking football' leans to spectacle, though from general knowledge he also stressed winning through the process, so he plays to win rather than to protect a result.

sis.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge the collective system came first (e.g. insisting Rivaldo play wide at Barcelona), consistent with verified set patterns.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge he wanted technically secure players for his possession game (verified) but also athletic, hard-running ones, with no room for a static number 10.

bas.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); scopeNote mentions youth players at Ajax, and from general knowledge he built the 1995 side on academy products (Kluivert, Seedorf, Davids) and later promoted Xavi and Puyol at Barcelona.

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge Van Gaal was a strict, authoritarian disciplinarian who clashed with stars and kept decisions to himself.
